About the local evidence

Recent records lead the list, then historical seasonal records, then UK guide candidates. Counts reflect recording activity, not abundance. The mushroom list excludes major lichen groups and several plant-disease fungi; it is not a complete local survey. Species with unknown ecology remain visible under “All habitats” or “Not documented yet”.

Observe, don’t identify by photo. This is a scouting guide. Photos do not establish identity or edibility. Never eat fungi based on this app.

mycelium · UK field companion

HOW TO READ YOUR REPORT

Better leads, with visible evidence.

Current ground conditions

Open-Meteo supplies hourly weather for the past 28 days and current modelled soil moisture. These are grid estimates, not rain gauges or soil probes in your wood. We exclude future hours. Today’s rain ends at the last completed hour, while current soil data can be newer. Midnight’s hourly rain belongs to the previous day. The overnight low covers 18:00 to 08:00; before 08:00 it is labelled “night so far”.

Soil moisture is volumetric water content: 20% means water occupies an estimated 20% of soil volume. It is not 20% saturation or a chance of finding fungi. Soil type affects the interpretation. The three-day trend helps distinguish rewetting from drying. Rain minus reference evapotranspiration over seven days is a drying cue, not a direct measurement of woodland water balance.

Conditions index, not percentage chance

The 0–100 index summarises broad scouting conditions. It does not estimate the probability of a species fruiting. Its exploratory weights are: seven-day rain, up to 30 points at 20 mm; wet days (≥0.5 mm per rolling 24 hours), up to 20 at four days; 24-hour humidity, 0–20 across 60–95%; mild 24-hour mean air temperature, up to 10; and three-day topsoil trend, 0–20 across −2 to +2 percentage points. Temperature ramps up from 2 to 10 °C and down from 18 to 28 °C. Subtract 15 for overnight frost, 10 when weekly rain minus reference evaporation is below −10 mm, and 5 for mean wind above 20 km/h with humidity below 70%. The final index is bounded to 0–100. Missing a required input means no score. These thresholds are app heuristics, not validated species-specific fruiting models.

What can actually be inferred?

Rain, temperature, humidity, soil moisture and longer drying periods influence fruiting, but host trees, soil, wood decay, mycelium and species biology also matter. A shower two days ago cannot reliably predict a particular flush. Large-scale fruiting research and British phenology research support considering season and longer weather history; they do not calibrate this daily index.

Local evidence and the species list

iNaturalist research-grade species counts within 30 km are fetched separately for the last 14 calendar days (including today) and the current month across all years. We retrieve up to six pages of 500 taxa per query and disclose a cap when reached. Lichen classes Lecanoromycetes, Arthoniomycetes, Lichinomycetes and Eurotiomycetes, and several microscopic plant-disease genera, are excluded from scouting results. This filter is approximate; unfamiliar macroscopic fungi are retained rather than restricted to the guide. Recent records outrank historical records. Neither source is a woodland survey; recording bias, delayed uploads and misidentifications remain possible.

The UK guide supplies additional seasonal habitat leads, even when no local record is returned. Source-linked entries include individual First Nature references. Other expanded guide notes are broad habitat guidance, not expert-validated species models. Common-name searches include dyer’s polypore/mazegill and slimy/beech milkcap. A common name never confirms your sighting.

Photos and sources

Reference photos are matched to scientific names, with reconciled synonyms, using iNaturalist taxon photos. Each detail view credits the photographer and links to the original. Surrey Wildlife Trust offers further local context. Weather by Open-Meteo (CC BY 4.0).

Offline and installation

Your last report, app shell and viewed photos are saved on this device. Weather older than six hours is marked stale; each evidence source keeps its fetch date. Refresh online before a walk. Coordinates are sent to Open-Meteo and iNaturalist; there is no app account or analytics. Clear site storage to remove saved data. Install from your Android browser’s menu, or in iPhone Safari use Share → Add to Home Screen. Private hosting authentication can affect offline starts.
